unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
Gregor, Sep 2025: Despite hopeful statements from the mayor of Coatzacoalcos in February 2024 speculating on CFE's future investment in the project, there has been no solid news about this export terminal since 2022. All recent media references have referred to CFE's project in the past tense ("CFE had previously announced a potential tender for an LNG facility for Coatzacoalcos"), and have focused instead on the private Coatzacoalcos II LNG export terminal currently being promoted by Comercializadora Aqualita, S.A. and CASARVE Servicios, S.R.L. 
In light of the above, I'm moving the CFE project from proposed to shelved.

GC, Sep 2024: No forward movement on this project since late 2022, although completion of the Southeast Gateway Pipeline in 2025 may give it a new lease on life; move to Shelved in 2025 if no further news?

GC, Sep 2025: No updates. Move to cancelled in Q4 2026 if no further news?

GC, Sep 2024: New Fortress Energy and Pemex cancelled their agreement for the Lakach project in November 2023, so I've moved it to Shelved.

unit_rows.LocalNames: Terminal de Exportación de GNL de Lakach

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit: GC, Sep 2024: New Fortress Energy reported first gas for Train 1 was achieved in July 2024, with commissioning, first cargo shipment, and full production all achieved in August 2024. I have changed the terminal's start-up date accordingly, from Nov 2023 to Aug 2024.
unit_rows.OtherNames: Altamira Fast LNG, Altamira Offshore LNG Hub

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
Gregor, Sep 2025: NFE's Q4 2024 Investor Presentation has pushed back the timeline for Train 2. Construction now expected to begin in Q3 2025, mechanical completion anticipated in Q4 2026, and commercial operation in H1 2027.

GC, Sep 2024: Owner NFE confirmed in July 2024 that is has obtained a loan to finance Train 2, and expects construction to be complete in the first half of 2026.
unit_rows.OtherNames: Altamira Fast LNG, Altamira Offshore LNG Hub
unit_rows.LocalNames: Terminal de Exportación de GNL New Fortress Altamira

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
Gregor, Sep 2025: New Fortress Energy's 2024 Form 10-K (p 63) indicates that the company still plans to deploy "up to two" additional 1.4 mtpa export units at the existing Altamira LNG Import Terminal (i.e. Trains 2 and 3). However, recent company documents have not specified a precise timeline for Train 3.

GC, Sep 2024: Train 3 was previously listed as under construction based on a May 2023 news story from Reuters. However, more recent documents from New Fortress Energy and other sources make it clear that only Train 2 is under construction. I've changed the status of Train 3 back to Proposed.
unit_rows.OtherNames: Altamira Fast LNG, Altamira Offshore LNG Hub
unit_rows.LocalNames: Terminal de Exportación de GNL New Fortress Altamira

unit_rows.ResearcherNotesUnit:
Gregor, Sep 2025: New Fortress Energy's 2024 Form 10-K (p 63) indicated that the company had scaled back its LNG export plans, noting that New Fortress would now only deploy "up to two" additional 1.4 mtpa export units at the existing Altamira LNG Import Terminal, as opposed to the "up to four" previously announced on p 60 of NFE's 2023 Form 10-K. As a result, I've changed status of Trains 4 and 5 to shelved. 

GC, Sep 2024: I've added trains 4 and 5 here based on New Fortress Energy's 2023 10-K filing with the SEC (see p 60 under the "Altamira" heading): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1749723/000174972324000011/nfe-20231231.htm
